prerequisites: Competencies obtained from services, networks, and distributed systems courses in the Bachelor's degree.
Proficiency in handling documentation in English is highly recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to understand and apply the operation and organization of the Internet, new generation network technologies and protocols, component models, middleware, and services.
Ability to design and evaluate operating systems and servers, and applications and systems based on distributed computing.
Be able to select the appropriate distributed application architecture for a given problem.
Know how to select the appropriate distributed application architecture for a given problem.
Know how to design a distributed application based on a specific architecture.
Understand and apply techniques for evaluating enterprise distributed applications.
Understand integration techniques for enterprise distributed applications.
Be able to apply integration techniques for enterprise distributed applications.
Be able to design applications and distributed systems based on cloud computing.
Be able to design applications and distributed systems based on grid computing.

syllabus_topics: Introduction. Needs and challenges of distributed systems.
Cloud services. IaaS, PaaS, SaaS, CaaS.
Acceleration of distributed systems using caches.
assessment_rules: For ordinary calls, continuous evaluation is used. Students must obtain a minimum of 5 out of 10 in each of the three assessments (theoretical test, practical assignments, group work). If all assessments meet this minimum, the final grade is calculated as 0.2*Teo + 0.2*Prac + 0.6*TG. For extraordinary calls, the group work grade from the ordinary call is used (contributing 40%), and a single comprehensive written exam for theoretical and practical knowledge is conducted (contributing 60%), which must be passed with at least 5 out of 10. If the group work was not completed in the ordinary call, the maximum grade in the extraordinary call is 6. Students under differentiated evaluation (part-time, blended, or non-presential) will have a final theory exam (0-5 points) and a final practical exam (0-5 points), with the final grade being the sum of both.
